function: D3QN agents learn 3D deployment of a RIS-UAV, per-user bandwidth allocation and (D3QN-Pure) RIS phase shifts to maximize energy efficiency; BS power by Dinkelbach (pp. 6-10).
system: Ground BS (M antennas), passive reflecting RIS on UAV (N = 8 to 12), K single-antenna users, 10 MHz; carrier band, M, K not stated (pp. 4, 11, 14).
method: Dueling double DQN (D3QN), 2 layers of 20 neurons, online reinforcement learning; D3QN-MM takes RIS phases from the MM algorithm, D3QN-Pure learns them (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user channels with path loss beta*d^-alpha (alpha 3.76), users random on ground; parameters from [17], [11]; no dataset (pp. 5, 11).
test_conditions: Trained and tested in one simulated scenario (120 time slots, convergence near 1250 to 1500 rounds); N varied 8 to 12; no unseen scenario reported (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Learned: DQN and DDQN with MM or learned phases ([16], [28]); non-learned: random RIS phases, average bandwidth, fixed UAV locations, AF relay (pp. 11-14).
metrics: Energy efficiency in Mbps/Joule (CDF over training), reward and energy efficiency versus training rounds, optimal 3D location, percent gain over AF relay (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Order O(|S1||A1| f_dink K^n f_MM N^m) for D3QN-MM and O(|S2||A2| f_dink K^n) for D3QN-Pure, eqs. (33)-(34); no runtime reported (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "are modeled as Rician channels" with path loss beta*d^-alpha; p. 11: the path-loss values "are taken from [17]" (Table III: alpha 3.76, beta 10^-3.53). Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 14: "we investigate the impact of the number of reflecting elements N on the energy efficiency" (N = 8 to 12, Fig. 13). This is a parameter sweep, and the state holds each phase shift (p. 9); the paper never reports testing a trained agent on a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 12: "accompanied by assigning random phase shifts to the RIS" (D3QN-RP, random RIS baseline); p. 11: "the two algorithms, DQN and DDQN, which are utilized in [16]"; p. 12: "These methods are documented in [28]"; all compared on energy efficiency (Figs. 8 to 11, pp. 13-14).
q4_support: p. 11: "Thus the complexity of the D3QN-MM algorithm is" O(|S1||A1| f_dink K^n f_MM N^m), eq. (33); D3QN-Pure is O(|S2||A2| f_dink K^n), eq. (34).
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulations were performed using Python 3.7.12" with TensorFlow. The paper has no code or data availability statement, no link or DOI, and the channels are simulated, not a public dataset.
notes: Area 6 chosen by the tie-break order (6 before 3): the learned control (bandwidth, RIS phase shifts in D3QN-Pure, UAV placement) acts on an aerial air-to-ground link through a RIS-UAV; area 3 also fits by function. In D3QN-MM the RIS phases come from the MM algorithm, and BS power comes from the Dinkelbach algorithm in both. q3: D3QN-RP (random phases) is taken as the non-learned baseline and DQN/DDQN of [16], [28] as the learned ones. M, K and the default N are not stated; N = 8 to 12 only in Fig. 13. Tables I, III, IV and Figs. 4 to 13 were read from the page images.
